Issue Description: USBDeviceImplementation::instance() is called in a static hotplug callback without a null check. If the singleton has not been initialised or has already been destroyed, instance() returns nullptr and the dereference causes undefined behaviour.
Suggested Fix: Add a null guard: auto* impl = USBDeviceImplementation::instance(); if (nullptr == impl) return 0; before calling any method on it.

Issue Description: Second call to instance() in the attached callback is also unguarded. The pointer could change between the two calls.
Suggested Fix: Use the guarded pointer from the first null check instead of calling instance() a second time.

Issue Description: USBDeviceImplementation::instance() called in the static detached callback without a null check, mirroring the same defect in libUSBHotPlugCallbackDeviceAttached.
Suggested Fix: Apply the same null-guard pattern as the fix for line 386.

Issue Description: Second unguarded instance() call in the detached callback. Same risk of double-deref without re-validation.
Suggested Fix: Reuse the guarded pointer obtained at the start of the callback.

Issue Description: libusb_get_active_config_descriptor allocates a config_desc structure on success, but libusb_free_config_descriptor is never called. This leaks memory on every call to getUSBDeviceInfoStructFromDeviceDescriptor.
Suggested Fix: Call libusb_free_config_descriptor(config_desc) after using config_desc and before the function returns.

Issue Description: The bool _handlingUSBDeviceEvents is written from libUSBClose (main thread) and read in libUSBEventsHandlingThread without any synchronisation primitive. This is a data race under the C++ memory model.
Suggested Fix: Declare _handlingUSBDeviceEvents as std::atomic<bool> to guarantee visibility and prevent data races.

Issue Description: The condition '4 < retValue' rejects a valid 4-byte response that encodes exactly one language ID (2-byte header + 2-byte language code). Devices with a single language ID are silently skipped.
Suggested Fix: Change the condition to '>= 4' (i.e., 'retValue >= 4') so that exactly one language ID is handled correctly.

Issue Description: LOGERR at line 664 is placed inside the 'if (4 < retValue)' branch, which is the success path. It is executed after manufacturer/product/serial extraction regardless of whether those succeeded, and uses a stale retValue from the language-ID descriptor call. This misleads diagnostics.
Suggested Fix: Remove this LOGERR or move it into the error branch (the enclosing else). The individual getUSBDescriptorValue calls already log their own errors.

Source Code Snippet: LOGERR("languageID: %u, libusb_get_string_descriptor failed: %s", languageID, libusb_strerror((enum libusb_error)retValue));
Issue Description: This LOGERR is executed unconditionally when the first libusb_get_string_descriptor fails, even when the ASCII fallback at lines 579-587 succeeds and status is set to ERROR_NONE. It incorrectly reports an error in the success-via-fallback case.
Suggested Fix: Move LOGERR inside the inner 'if (retValue < 0)' block at line 580 so it only fires when the ASCII fallback also fails.

Issue Description: A local 'serialNumber' variable is declared inside the LIBUSB_CLASS_MASS_STORAGE branch of getUSBDeviceInfoStructFromDeviceDescriptor but is never used. The actual serial number is written to pUSBDeviceInfo->serialNumber by getDevicePathFromDevice.
Suggested Fix: Remove the unused 'string serialNumber;' variable declaration.

Issue Description: In GetDeviceList the loop variable 'status' retains the result of the last device iteration. If any intermediate device fails but the last succeeds, earlier errors are lost. Conversely, if the last device fails but earlier ones succeeded, the iterator is not created even though valid data was collected.
Suggested Fix: Track success per-device separately. Always create the iterator if at least one device was processed successfully, independent of the last device status.

Issue Description: The fixed-size char path[256] buffer may truncate if PLUGIN_USBDEVICE_PATH + sysfsPath + "/serial" exceeds 255 characters. Truncation silently produces a wrong path without any diagnostic.
Suggested Fix: Use std::string concatenation or verify the total length before snprintf. Alternatively, log a warning if snprintf returns >= sizeof(path).

Source Code Snippet: auto MoveFile(const string &from, const string &to) -> bool
Issue Description: MoveFile is a non-inline free function defined in a header file. If this header is included in more than one translation unit, the linker will see multiple definitions and either fail or silently pick one (undefined behaviour under ODR).
Suggested Fix: Mark the function inline, or move its definition to a .cpp file.

Source Code Snippet: bool getLastLine(const std::string& input, std::string& res_str)
Issue Description: getLastLine is a non-inline free function defined in a header file, subject to the same ODR violation risk as MoveFile.
Suggested Fix: Mark the function inline, or move its definition to a .cpp file.
